data.narrative:
Claros, a Seed-stage climate and energy company founded by Daniel Kultran and Grant Verstandig, has raised $30M to date. The broader Climate & Energy sector comprises one public comparable (LNZA) and eight private peers including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix. However, the peer set lacks sufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables with similar valuation tier to support reliable multiples-based analysis.

The valuation rests on stage-progression methodology. Using total capital raised as a proxy anchor of $30M and applying a typical 2.5x step-up multiplier from Seed to the subsequent financing round yields an implied valuation of $75M. This multiplier reflects historical median progression in early-stage venture without sector-specific adjustment, as the peer universe does not furnish enough tight comparables to narrow the range meaningfully.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $64M (low) to $86M (high), centered at $75M. This range reflects ±15% sensitivity around the stage-progression result. Key uncertainties include the absence of recent Seed-to-Series A valuation step-ups specific to climate-tech, limited visibility into Claros' revenue traction or unit economics relative to the broader peer set, and macro dependency of clean energy venture returns on policy and commodity price volatility. Additional comparable data at similar deployment stage would materially tighten confidence in this estimate.
